target.meaning: Validate interannual crop-risk and spatial uncertainty inputs for a 1337 low-input physical model. These records do not define absolute population capacity or replace exact-location crop physics.

sources.title: Three centuries of English crop yields, 1211-1491 / Medieval Crop Yields Database
sources.provider: Bruce Campbell, Queen's University Belfast; British Agricultural History Society
sources.citation: Campbell, B.; Livingstone, M.; Drewery, A.; Whittick, C.; Yeates, E. (2007), Three centuries of English crop yields, 1211 1491, Queen's University Belfast.

coverage.geography: England, named demesne farms and regional/manorial chronologies

evidence: The dataset contains annually dated yields for individual field crops on individual English demesne farms derived from manorial accounts.
The BAHS regional chronologies weight changing regional coverage; manorial chronologies are unweighted and are explicitly preferred for annual variation.
Chronologies are annual, net of seed, gross of tithe, indexed to the 1270-1429 mean, and publish the number of observations available in each year.
The database is strongest for validating year-to-year yield risk and spatial sampling variance in medieval England, not peasant-wide absolute output.
allowed_uses: Estimate empirical annual yield anomaly distributions by crop family.
Compare regional versus farm-level variance and observation-count weighting.
Validate the sign and relative magnitude of climate-risk responses when joined to OWDA or documentary climate records.
Hold out named regional chronologies to test spatial generalization.
forbidden_uses: Do not treat demesne yields as a global peasant yield target.
Do not use the indexed series as an absolute kg/ha label without preserving its seed/tithe semantics and a separate absolute-yield bridge.
Do not use starting population or food prices as yield labels.

independence.shared_source_risk: Regional and manorial chronologies derive from the same underlying account database; split them by source family, not as independent observations.

acquisition.required_next_step: Download the raw observations and chronology tables, record checksum, map farm/region names to EU5 geometry, and preserve observation counts.

sources.title: Old World Drought Atlas
sources.provider: Cook et al.; NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
sources.citation: Cook, E. R. et al. (2015), Old World megadroughts and pluvials during the Common Era, Science Advances 1, e1500561.
evidence: NOAA describes year-to-year tree-ring reconstructed summer wetness and dryness with spatially complete maps over Europe and the Mediterranean.
The reconstruction includes medieval megadroughts and pluvials and is explicitly intended to place hydroclimatic variability in historical perspective.
The Climate Data Guide warns that grid-point reconstruction skill varies and recommends using calibration/validation statistics; regional patterns can be more reliable than individual grid cells.
allowed_uses: Derive spatially correlated drought-risk scenarios for EU5 footprints.
Validate whether simulated crop-risk tails co-occur in historically documented European drought years.
Use grid-point calibration/validation skill as an uncertainty weight, never as an unrecorded fill.
forbidden_uses: Do not convert PDSI directly into kg/ha without an independently fitted crop response.
Do not treat every 0.5-degree cell as equally observed or equally skilled.

independence.shared_proxy_risk: Tree-ring reconstructions may share chronologies or climate teleconnections with other drought atlases; do not count atlas families as independent yield observations.

acquisition.required_next_step: Fetch PDSI, reconstruction skill, and missing-value layers; sample them at calibrated EU5 footprints and retain skill/missingness columns.

sources.title: Monsoon Asia Drought Atlas
sources.provider: Cook, Anchukaitis, Buckley, D'Arrigo, Jacoby and Wright; NOAA WDS
sources.citation: Cook, E. R. et al. (2010), Asian monsoon variability over the past millennium, Science 328, 486-489; NOAA DOI 10.25921/b8gk-7h90.

coverage.resolution: 534 grid-point reconstructions on a 2.5 x 2.5 degree grid; JJA PDSI

evidence: NOAA reports an annual/seasonal gridded reconstruction back to 1300 CE, based on Asian tree-ring data.
The archived product is an ensemble of reconstructions using multiple search radii and correlation weightings; weak verification areas are explicitly documented.
allowed_uses: Validate monsoon-season drought tail frequency and spatial correlation in East and South Asia.
Use only grid points with documented skill or aggregate to regional scales where the atlas guidance supports it.
forbidden_uses: Do not use MADA as an absolute harvest or population target.
Do not silently extrapolate MADA beyond its monsoon-domain footprint.

independence.shared_proxy_risk: Both are PDSI reconstructions and should be treated as climate evidence, not independent crop labels.

acquisition.required_next_step: Fetch JJA PDSI and reconstruction skill metadata; map the 2.5-degree cells to EU5 locations and identify gaps in South/Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Patterns in extreme droughts/floods and harvest grades in eastern China, 801-1910
sources.provider: Hao, Wu, Zheng, Chen, Zhang and Luo; Climate of the Past
sources.citation: Hao, Z. et al. (2020), Climate of the Past 16, 101-116, https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-16-101-2020.

coverage.geography: Eastern China, 63 historical stations grouped into North China Plain, Jianghuai and Jiangnan
coverage.spatial_resolution: Station areas represent approximately 20 counties; three regional aggregates

evidence: The study reconstructs annual drought/flood grades at 63 stations from official histories, chronicles and local gazettes.
It also reconstructs grain harvest grades and food-security responses; harvest grades are relative to an expected maximum rather than absolute kg/ha.
The study evaluates confidence from the fraction of years with data in 50-year windows and reports significantly poorer harvest grades in extreme drought years.
The source itself warns that documentary compilation and reconstruction steps create independence and consistency limitations.
allowed_uses: Test whether crop-risk scenarios produce lower relative harvests during documented drought years.
Validate spatial aggregation at North China Plain/Jianghuai/Jiangnan scale.
Use the published confidence/missingness assessment to widen uncertainty.
forbidden_uses: Do not use harvest grades as absolute yield or population-capacity labels.
Do not treat the 63 stations as independent observations when derived from shared documentary compilations.

independence.shared_source_risk: The drought and harvest series share historical-document sources; use them for paired event validation, not independent likelihood factors.

acquisition.required_next_step: Download the supplement, preserve ordinal grades and confidence, and build an exact eastern-China EU5 crosswalk before using it in validation.

sources.title: Reassessing long-term drought risk and societal impacts in Shenyang, 1200-2015
sources.provider: Tang, Macdonald, Sangster, Chiverrell and Gaulton; Climate of the Past
sources.citation: Tang, L. et al. (2020), Climate of the Past 16, 1917-1935, https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-16-1917-2020.
evidence: The paper combines a reconstructed precipitation series with historical documentary accounts to extend drought analysis back to 1200 CE.
It is a useful local severity/duration case but not an annual yield series and not a regional population target.
allowed_uses: Validate event timing, drought duration and local downscaling behavior.
forbidden_uses: Do not use as a China-wide or crop-yield target.

acquisition.required_next_step: Acquire article supplement and map the Shenyang selector to EU5.

sources.title: North American Drought Atlas v2a
sources.citation: Cook et al. North American Drought Atlas v2a, NOAA NCEI drought variability archive.
evidence: NOAA reports annual summer PDSI reconstructions over 0-2006 CE; atlas guidance documents calibration/validation skill requirements.
allowed_uses: Validate drought-frequency tails and spatial correlation in North American EU5 locations.
forbidden_uses: Do not infer crop yield or absolute capacity directly from PDSI.

acquisition.required_next_step: Fetch PDSI and skill layers and perform EU5 crosswalk.

sources.title: South American Drought Atlas
sources.citation: Morales, M. S. et al. (2020), Six hundred years of South American tree rings reveal an increase in severe hydroclimatic events since mid-20th century, NOAA DOI 10.25921/b1ps-rw37.

coverage.geography: South America south of 12 degrees south

evidence: NOAA describes a 286-record tree-ring network and annual summer soil-moisture reconstruction from 1400 CE.
allowed_uses: Hold out South American drought-risk tails and spatial covariance for the 1400-1500 overlap.
forbidden_uses: Do not use to set 1337 global scale; the record starts 63 years after game start.

acquisition.required_next_step: Acquire scPDSI and skill fields and map only 1400-1500 validation years.

sources.title: Eastern Australia and New Zealand Drought Atlas
sources.citation: Palmer, J. G. et al. (2015/2016), Eastern Australia and New Zealand Drought Atlas, NOAA DOI 10.25921/7qpw-x384.

coverage.resolution: 0.5 x 0.5 degree austral-summer PDSI; 176 tree-ring chronologies and one coral series

evidence: NOAA reports a gridded drought reconstruction beginning in 1500 CE, with documented historical-event validation.
allowed_uses: Use only as a boundary-year/late-window holdout; it cannot calibrate 1337 uncertainty.
forbidden_uses: Do not treat 1500 as evidence for the 1337 state or global scale.

acquisition.required_next_step: Acquire data and keep it in a validation-only fold.

sources.title: Global Dataset of Historical Yield of Major Crops v1.2
sources.citation: Iizumi, T. (2017), Global dataset of historical yield of major crops v1.2, DIAS DOI 10.20783/DIAS.528.
evidence: The dataset is a satellite vegetation-index and FAO country-statistics hybrid, with time-constant 2000 harvested-area weights; it is not a medieval observation.
allowed_uses: Check whether the crop-water response implementation produces plausible relative yield variability under observed climate.
forbidden_uses: Do not train 1337 absolute yields, land shares or population capacity with this source.

acquisition.required_next_step: Only use in an explicitly modern diagnostic fold if needed; keep out of 1337 acceptance metrics.

blockers: No comparable direct annual yield database has been located for continental Europe in 1100-1500; English demesne records are not globally representative.
Chinese harvest grades are ordinal/relative rather than kg per hectare; South Asia, Southeast Asia and Central Asia remain under-covered.
SADA begins in 1400 and NADA is hydroclimate only; no direct 1100-1337 annual yield series is verified here.
No annually resolved, spatially mappable 1100-1500 crop-yield or drought atlas covering African EU5 locations was verified. Do not use modern African yield statistics as medieval risk labels.
ANZDA starts in 1500 and is validation-only; no 1100-1337 annual yield-risk source was verified.

direct_yield_risk: Use MCYDB annual anomalies and observation counts for England; separate regional weighted chronologies from unweighted manorial variance.
Use Hao et al. relative harvest grades as one-sided/event validation in eastern China, preserving ordinal semantics.
Never create location-level historical capacity targets from either source.
climate_to_yield: Join independent historical yield records to OWDA/MADA or documentary drought years only after matching calendars and mapped boundaries.
Fit/validate only a bounded relative response or tail-frequency diagnostic; keep GAEZ/PyAEZ absolute yield as the physical baseline.
Use source-family holdouts: England manorial accounts, Chinese documentary harvests, and each drought-atlas family are not exchangeable observations.
spatial_uncertainty: Sample atlas grid-cell skill, missingness and reconstruction covariance at EU5 footprint points.
Use MCYDB farm-vs-regional variance to test aggregation error; do not substitute a global variance multiplier.
Aggregate to regional holdouts where grid-point reconstruction skill is weak.
parameter_uncertainty: Propagate empirical English yield anomaly quantiles and crop-specific source uncertainty separately from climate uncertainty.
Treat Chinese harvest grades as ordinal likelihood constraints, not continuous yield parameters.
Do not infer Africa, South Asia, or tropical crop parameter distributions from European cereals.

blocking_gaps: No raw direct-yield table has yet been downloaded, hashed and mapped to EU5; metadata verification alone cannot satisfy the annual-risk gate.
The existing annual simulation audit remains blocked because resolved crop parameter mappings and exact 101-year annual labels are absent.
Africa and much of South/Southeast/Central Asia lack independent 1100-1500 annual yield observations; no statistical or regional imputation is permitted.
Drought-atlas skill/missingness layers have not yet been acquired and must be carried into uncertainty.
The current fallback's climate response is not a substitute for a completed PyAEZ crop parameter registry.

acceptance.reason: The registry establishes the best available evidence and exact next acquisition steps, but it does not pretend that metadata or climate proxies close the missing direct-yield and crop-parameter labels.
